identification.summary: Cloudflare's Cloudforce One tracks FlyingYeti as a Russia-aligned threat actor that primarily targets Ukrainian defense entities and whose TTPs closely resemble those of UAC-0149, a cluster CERT-UA tracked earlier [S1][S3]. Cloudflare says that since 2024-04-26 it has taken measures to stop the actor launching a phishing espionage campaign; secondary coverage dates its detection to 2024-04-18, which the primary report does not confirm [S1][S5]. The campaign used debt-themed lures, a WinRAR exploit (CVE-2023-38831) and the COOKBOX PowerShell malware [S1][S2]. Microsoft says its Storm-1837 designation overlaps with activity other providers track as Flying Yeti and lists UAC-0149 [S4].
identification.firstObserved: SOC Prime, summarizing CERT-UA, reports UAC-0149 activity against Ukraine since at least autumn 2023 [S3]. Microsoft says Storm-1837 targeting of Ukrainian military devices was observed since December 2023 [S4]. Cloudflare's own FlyingYeti reporting centers on April-May 2024 [S1].
identification.notes: Name mapping rests on vendor statements of overlap, not on identical datasets. Cloudflare says FlyingYeti TTPs closely resemble UAC-0149 [S1]. Microsoft says Storm-1837 overlaps with Flying Yeti and lists UAC-0149 [S4]. Microsoft's name is a temporary 'Storm' designation, not a finalized weather-themed name [S4]. Do not merge facts across the three vendor clusters without the primary reports.

attribution.sponsor: No state sponsor or specific organization is named in the sources gathered. Cloudflare describes the actor as Russia-aligned [S1]; Microsoft describes Storm-1837 as Russia-based [S4].
attribution.confidence: Cloudflare states the group's activity suggests alignment with Russian interests [S1]. Microsoft calls Storm-1837 a Russia-based actor without naming a government entity [S4]. No government attribution was found.
attribution.basis: Cloudflare cites Russian-language code comments and operational hours matching the UTC+3 time zone, per secondary coverage of its report [S5]. TTP resemblance to CERT-UA's UAC-0149 [S1][S3]. Targeting of Ukrainian military entities [S1][S4].

objectives: Espionage against Ukrainian military and defense-related personnel, including access to devices used by drone operators [S1][S4]. Cloudflare describes the 2024 campaign as phishing espionage that also reached civilian targets [S1][S2].

regions: Ukraine; Cloudflare says about 94% of targeted devices were in Ukraine [S2]
targeting.notes: Cloudflare says the group mostly targets Ukrainian military entities and that this campaign pushed into civilian targets [S1][S2]. Full victim count is unknown because the campaign was disrupted early [S2]. Microsoft says Storm-1837 focuses on devices used by Ukrainian drone operators [S4].

capabilities.summary: Phishing delivered by email and Signal messages, using RAR archives that exploit WinRAR CVE-2023-38831 to run a script that opens a decoy and launches PowerShell tied to COOKBOX [S2][S3]. COOKBOX is a PowerShell backdoor that runs further commands; it sends an identifier in the X-Cookie HTTP header, persists through a registry Run key, and uses dynamic DNS (reported as NoIP) and Cloudflare Workers for C2 [S3]. Cloudflare reports the actor used Cloudflare Workers to fetch a WinRAR file hosted on GitHub, and decoy pages hosted on GitHub mimicking Kyiv's Komunalka housing site [S2][S5]. Microsoft says Storm-1837 uses a range of PowerShell backdoors (one called Cookbox by CERT-UA) and an Android backdoor, Griselda, which CERT-UA says is based on the Hydra banking malware and collects cookies, contacts and keystrokes [S4]. Cloudflare says its disruption stretched the actor's timeline from days to weeks and cost one instance nearly eight hours of debugging [S2][S5].

campaigns.name: Storm-1837 targeting of Ukrainian military devices
campaigns.summary: Microsoft says it observed Storm-1837 targeting Ukrainian military devices, with a focus on drone operators, since December 2023.

campaigns.name: Storm-1837 backdoor reused by Secret Blizzard
campaigns.summary: Microsoft says a Storm-1837 backdoor on a Ukrainian military device was configured to use the Telegram API and a Mega account, and assesses it was likely used by Secret Blizzard to deploy the Tavdig loader and KazuarV2. Microsoft says it is still investigating how Secret Blizzard gained control of the backdoor.

campaigns.name: UAC-0149 Signal lure to military personnel
campaigns.summary: SOC Prime, summarizing CERT-UA, reports a targeted attack on Ukraine's Armed Forces around the turn of 2024 using COOKBOX delivered via fake Signal messages (an XLS lure). The exact date and CERT-UA alert number were not confirmed.

campaigns.name: FlyingYeti debt-themed WinRAR/COOKBOX campaign
campaigns.summary: Cloudflare says that since 2024-04-26 it has acted to prevent FlyingYeti launching a phishing campaign (secondary coverage says detection was 2024-04-18) using spoofed payment notices that exploited fear of losing housing and utilities after Ukraine's eviction and utility-cutoff moratorium ended in January 2024. A malicious RAR exploited CVE-2023-38831 to run a CMD file delivering COOKBOX. SOC Prime reports CERT-UA issued an alert on 2024-04-18 on a new UAC-0149 COOKBOX wave.

campaigns.name: Cloudflare disruption and public report
campaigns.summary: Cloudflare says it acted against the campaign from late April, disrupted it in mid-May as the actor was about to deploy the final COOKBOX payload, and published its findings on 2024-05-30 using detections, code takedowns and third-party cooperation.

diamond.adversary: Russia-aligned (Cloudflare) or Russia-based (Microsoft) actor, tracked as FlyingYeti, UAC-0149 and Storm-1837; no sponsor named [S1][S4].
diamond.capability: Phishing via email and Signal, CVE-2023-38831 WinRAR exploit, COOKBOX PowerShell backdoor, Griselda Android backdoor [S2][S3][S4].
diamond.infrastructure: Cloudflare Workers, GitHub-hosted decoy pages and archives, dynamic DNS, and in one Microsoft-observed case Telegram API and Mega [S2][S3][S4][S5].
diamond.victim: Ukrainian military personnel and drone operators, plus civilians targeted by debt-themed lures; about 94% of targeted devices in Ukraine [S1][S2][S4].
diamond.socioPolitical: Exploits Ukrainian financial stress after the moratorium on evictions and utility cutoffs ended, in the context of Russian-aligned espionage against Ukraine's military [S1][S5].
diamond.technology: Unpatched WinRAR, PowerShell and script hosts on Windows endpoints, Signal as a delivery channel to military users, and Android devices used by operators [S3][S4].

gaps: Cloudflare's primary report could not be opened directly in this session; Cloudflare details come from search-result excerpts and secondary coverage (The Register, Dark Reading, The Hacker News, SOC Prime) [S2][S5].
CERT-UA's original alerts (the early-2024 and 2024-04-18 alerts) were not opened; SOC Prime is a secondary source and cites CERT-UA#9522 for the April alert [S3].
No government attribution, sponsor organization or personnel were found; Russia-alignment rests on vendor inference [S1][S4].
Whether FlyingYeti, UAC-0149 and Storm-1837 are identical clusters is not established beyond vendor statements of overlap [S1][S4].
How Secret Blizzard gained control of the Storm-1837 backdoor is unresolved per Microsoft [S4].
Activity after mid-2024 was not found in the sources gathered.
Griselda was not corroborated in a CERT-UA primary document in this session [S4].

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: Key terrain is the personal and unit-level devices of Ukrainian (and potentially partner) operators, especially messaging apps such as Signal, plus Windows endpoints with outdated archive software [S3][S4]. STEP 2: The actor exploits local socio-economic stress (debt, utilities) and impersonates municipal services, and uses commodity cloud services (Cloudflare Workers, GitHub, dynamic DNS) that blend into normal traffic [S2][S5]. STEP 3: Template is lure via Signal or email, then malicious RAR using CVE-2023-38831, then script and PowerShell COOKBOX, then registry persistence and C2 with X-Cookie identifier [S2][S3]. STEP 4: MLCOA is continued espionage phishing against Ukrainian military and drone-operator personnel with topical lures. MDCOA is use of the same delivery against partner-nation personnel supporting Ukraine, or hand-off of access to a more capable actor, as Microsoft observed when Secret Blizzard reused a Storm-1837 backdoor [S4]. Candidate indicators: WinRAR spawning cmd or PowerShell, new Run-key entries launching PowerShell, HTTP requests with an X-Cookie header to workers.dev or dynamic-DNS hosts, and GitHub-hosted decoy pages impersonating local services [S2][S3].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: track CERT-UA and vendor reporting on UAC-0149 and Storm-1837 and map to one tracking entry with noted overlaps [S1][S4]. (2) Authorities: any defensive action against third-party cloud services (GitHub, Cloudflare) should proceed through provider abuse channels and established legal authorities, as Cloudflare's own takedowns did [S2]. (3) Mission assurance: patch archive tools, restrict powershell.exe, wscript.exe, cscript.exe and mshta.exe per CERT-UA guidance, and brief personnel on messaging-app lures [S3]. (4) Coordination: share indicators with partners, since Microsoft shows a lower-tier actor's access can be reused by a stronger actor [S4].

provenance.importedSummary: FlyingYeti is a Russia-aligned threat actor targeting Ukrainian military entities. They conduct reconnaissance activities and launch phishing campaigns using malware like COOKBOX. FlyingYeti exploits the WinRAR vulnerability CVE-2023-38831 to infect targets with malicious payloads. Cloudforce One has successfully disrupted their operations and provided recommendations for defense against their phishing campaigns.
